newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SURANYI SAUS HUNGARY 1997 GDP TO EXCEED 3.0 PCT.
newsitem.headline: SURANYI SAUS HUNGARY 1997 GDP TO EXCEED 3.0 PCT.

text.p: Hungary's central bank chairman said he expected Hungary's 1997 GDP growth to exceed the government's target of 2.5 to 3.0 percent despite new figures showing a fall in GDP growth in the first quarter.
"Growth for the current year will be higher than three percent," Gyorgy Suranyi told Reuters Financial Television in an interview broadcast on Thursday.
The Central Statistical Office (KSH) said on Tuesday that the growth of the gross domestic product (GDP) slowed to 1.2 percent in the first quarter of 1997 from three percent in the previous quarter.
Analysts said the first quarter GDP figure was not disappointing since domestic consumption and investments were likely to pick up through the year.
Suranyi said GDP growth was based on improved exports and would therefore not result in a deterioration of the trade balance.
"(Growth) is accelerating without having any deterioration over the external account since the whole growth is basically export-led," he said.
Hungary's industry and trade ministry said on Wednesday both exports and imports grew between 10 and 13 percent in the first five months of this year.
